- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; add 0.5–1.5% to early-term forecasts.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows persistent bias toward lower values when sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.67); apply a 1–2% upward adjustment to align with true mean.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from bullish to bearish), model often fails to adjust; delay forecast correction until sentiment stabilizes or add a 1–2% downward buffer.
